key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cell losses occur and turn those losses into practical design rules for better device efficiency.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a common framework to compare BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes, fit real I–V data, and prioritize fixes such as improved junctions, co-catalysts, or nanostructuring.
method: Builds a physics-based loss model for light absorption, carrier transport, recombination, and interfacial transfer.
Generates ideal and real current-voltage curves plus efficiency maps to show theoretical limits and material-selection windows.
Uses experimental I–V fitting and Sankey diagrams to decompose energy losses and visualize solar-to-chemical conversion.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated against literature data across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Its diagnostic power depends on the quality of experimental I–V data and how well the model assumptions match a given device architecture.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
